recommendation_summary: Ship no new services or topics this week. Change the endpoint so PostgreSQL computes count(*) for the customer's unpaid invoices. Add a partial index only if EXPLAIN ANALYZE still shows a slow plan, and compare the plans before and after on production-sized data. It offers no optional additions and leaves no stated need unmet.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You need the unpaid-invoice count to return in under one second and to reflect committed invoices at request time.
labels.Deleted: Kafka topics, a CQRS projection, and Redis. No stated requirement needs them, and an asynchronous projection would break the request-time freshness requirement. Approved budget and peer trends are not requirements.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint loads every unpaid invoice row and builds an object for each one, only to count them in application memory.
labels.Checked myself: Only what you told me. I have not seen the code, the query plan, or the row counts.

note: The four record lines come before a bounded fix that counts in the database and keeps the count current at request time, and the reply rejects Kafka, CQRS and Redis by name.
